_about: Small bundled sample of well-known, version-detectable vulnerabilities (build step 4). Matching is by nmap's product/version strings, so treat hits as 'probable': Linux distributions often backport fixes without changing the upstream version number. Live NVD lookups (step 11) extend this. Fields: product = case-insensitive regex on nmap's product; ranges = list of [min_inclusive, max_exclusive] ('' = unbounded); 'exact' versions alternatively. distro_fixes: package revisions from Ubuntu/Debian security advisories that fixed the CVE for a given upstream version (compared with the revision in the service banner, e.g. 'OpenSSH 8.9p1 Ubuntu 3ubuntu0.10').

entries.title: vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor
entries.description: The vsftpd 2.3.4 source archive was replaced with a backdoored copy in 2011. Logging in with a username ending in ':)' opens a root shell on TCP port 6200.
entries.remediation: Replace vsftpd with a current version from your distribution and treat the host as compromised: rebuild it from a clean image.
entries.fixed_in: Any build other than the tampered 2.3.4 archive (e.g. 2.3.5 or later)

entries.title: ProFTPD 1.3.5 mod_copy unauthenticated file copy
entries.description: mod_copy's SITE CPFR/CPTO commands work without logging in, letting anyone copy files on the server, for example placing a PHP shell in the web root.
entries.remediation: Upgrade ProFTPD to 1.3.5a or later, or disable mod_copy.

entries.title: OpenSSH regreSSHion (signal handler race)
entries.description: A race condition in sshd's SIGALRM handler can allow unauthenticated remote code execution as root on glibc-based Linux. Exploitation is slow and timing-dependent, but practical.
entries.remediation: Update OpenSSH to 9.8p1 or later (or your distribution's patched package; Debian/Ubuntu backported the fix without changing the 8.x/9.x version). As a stopgap set LoginGraceTime 0 in sshd_config (this trades the RCE risk for easier connection exhaustion).

entries.title: OpenSSH username enumeration
entries.description: Differences in how sshd answers malformed public-key authentication requests reveal whether a username exists, helping an attacker target password guessing.
entries.remediation: Upgrade OpenSSH to 7.8 or later; use key-only authentication and fail2ban or similar rate limiting.

entries.title: Apache 2.4.49 path traversal
entries.description: A flaw in path normalization lets crafted URLs (encoded '../') read files outside the document root, and run commands if mod_cgi is enabled.
entries.remediation: Upgrade Apache httpd to 2.4.51 or later. Make sure 'Require all denied' protects the filesystem root.

entries.title: Apache 2.4.49/2.4.50 path traversal and RCE
entries.description: The fix for CVE-2021-41773 in 2.4.50 was incomplete: double-encoded traversal still reaches files outside the web root, and leads to remote code execution with mod_cgi.
entries.remediation: Upgrade Apache httpd to 2.4.51 or later.

entries.title: Apache mod_proxy HTTP request smuggling
entries.description: Some mod_proxy configurations using RewriteRule or ProxyPassMatch with user-supplied URL data allow request smuggling, bypassing access controls on the proxy. Only affects servers using that configuration.
entries.remediation: Upgrade Apache httpd to 2.4.56 or later.

entries.title: nginx resolver off-by-one
entries.description: When the 'resolver' directive is used, a crafted DNS response can cause a 1-byte memory overwrite, crashing the worker and possibly allowing code execution.
entries.remediation: Upgrade nginx to 1.20.1 / 1.21.0 or later, or avoid the resolver directive.

entries.title: Exim 'Return of the WIZard' remote command execution
entries.description: Improper validation of recipient addresses lets a remote attacker run commands as root in default configurations.

entries.title: dnsmasq DNS heap overflow
entries.description: A crafted DNS response causes a heap overflow in dnsmasq (common on routers), allowing remote code execution.
entries.remediation: Update the router firmware or dnsmasq to 2.78 or later. If the vendor no longer ships updates, replace the device.

entries.title: SambaCry: shared-library upload to RCE
entries.description: A client with write access to a share can upload a shared library and make smbd load it, running code as root. Patched in 4.4.14, 4.5.10 and 4.6.4; this check flags everything below 4.6.4, so verify the exact branch.
entries.remediation: Upgrade Samba, or set 'nt pipe support = no' in smb.conf as a workaround.

entries.title: Samba usermap_script command injection
entries.description: With 'username map script' enabled, shell metacharacters in the username are executed during login.
entries.remediation: Upgrade Samba (3.0.25 is ancient: replace the host or its OS).

entries.title: Dropbear format-string vulnerability
entries.description: A format-string bug in Dropbear (common in embedded devices and routers) can allow remote code execution.
entries.remediation: Update the device firmware or Dropbear to 2016.74 or later.

entries.title: IIS 6.0 WebDAV ScStoragePathFromUrl overflow
entries.description: A buffer overflow in IIS 6.0's WebDAV service allows remote code execution. Windows Server 2003 has been out of support since 2015.
entries.remediation: Retire Windows Server 2003 / IIS 6.0. If impossible, disable WebDAV.
entries.fixed_in: None: IIS 6.0 / Windows Server 2003 is end-of-life

entries.title: UnrealIRCd 3.2.8.1 backdoor
entries.description: Some UnrealIRCd 3.2.8.1 downloads contained a backdoor that runs any command sent after the prefix 'AB;'.
entries.remediation: Remove this build, install a current IRC daemon from a trusted source, and treat the host as compromised.
entries.fixed_in: Re-released clean 3.2.8.1 archive, or later versions

entries.title: distcc daemon runs arbitrary commands
entries.description: distccd without access restrictions executes compile 'jobs' sent by anyone, which can be any command.
entries.remediation: Stop distccd, or restrict it with --allow to trusted build hosts only and firewall port 3632.
entries.fixed_in: No code fix: restrict access with --allow and a firewall
